Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Marcus and I attached our proposed redlines to the DPA (attached: Crosstec_DPA_Redlines.docx) and an initial version of the dataflow exhibit we drafted to show the systems and hosting regions (attached: RI_DPA_Exhibit_Dataflow.xlsx).

Two asks up front: 
- Can Redwood confirm whether the SCCs you propose will be executed as the standard EU transfer mechanism for our contract (we're in the UK/EU footprint)? If not, can you confirm which mechanism Redwood prefers and whether there are additional signing steps?
- We flagged a couple of operational questions in the exhibit about "edge export paths" and "prefix/KV cache routing" — those are in the exhibit worksheet tab labeled "OPERATIONS". We want to ensure the exhibit correctly represents where cached prompts/keys are persisted and whether that affects transfer obligations.

High-level timeline we'd like: legal redline sync next week, followed by final DPA signature within two weeks if all is aligned. We're sensitive to hosting locality and processor role allocation. Marcus will be available for a technical call on Friday afternoon BST.

Thanks — attaching the redlines and a simple PDF export of the SCC mapping for your review (SCCs-mapping.pdf).

Best,
Natalie Cross
Head of Security & Privacy
Crosstec Analytics

Natalie — thanks for the materials, received and reviewed at a high level.

Action plan from our side: 
1) I will coordinate the legal sync and propose two time slots next week for Sean/Laura + your counsel.
2) Looping in Ben (privacy/contracts) to run a redline pass on the DPA clauses and SCCs mapping to confirm which mechanism we will sign.
3) Laura, can you confirm the hosting region/Private package options that map to the exhibit sheet (specifically the OPERATIONS tab flags)?

Ben — quick note on things to prioritize in the redline: processor/controller language for subprocessing, the SCCs adoption clause (we need to confirm if execution will be standard SCCs as-is or SCCs + supplementary protections), and an explicit section for export routes when prefix caching/edge routing is in use.

Natalie — we want to be transparent about typical timeline risks: if there are significant redlines to the SCCs we may propose a short addendum (transfer-impact addendum) instead of replacing the SCCs wholesale; that is often faster operationally. We'll document tradeoffs in the call.

I'll send availability separately.

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Folks — quick redline summary after an initial pass (see attached notes inline in Crosstec_DPA_Redlines.docx):

1) SCCs: Redwood's standard practice for customers in the EU/UK is to execute the European Commission SCCs (saliently the 2021 modular clauses) and then adopt a transfer-impact assessment where appropriate. We can sign the SCCs as a mechanism; for any dataflow that involves non-EU residual KV caches (edge caching), we'll surface that in a transfer-impact addendum.

Suggested language for the DPA (to propose in the legal sync): 
- Replace current Section 4.2 with: "Where the parties rely on the SCCs for cross-border transfers, the parties agree to execute the 2021 SCCs in the form attached as Exhibit B. Any operational routes that could result in transfers to third countries will be documented in a Transfer-Impact Addendum to be agreed within 21 days of execution."

2) Processor roles & subprocessor notice: Request to tighten the notice windows in the order form — propose 10 days for notification and 30 days for objection (we can set an internal escalation path if objection is raised).

3) Operational evidence: For the OPERATIONS tab items (edge export paths and prefix/KV cache), we will prepare a short technical appendix that states: what is cached, retention window, where persistence occurs (region), and whether the cache qualifies as a "transfer" under GDPR. I've attached RI_DPA_Exhibit_Dataflow.xlsx with inline comments where I need Crosstec confirmation on two caches marked with TODO.

Next steps: 
- Laura: confirm region mapping and whether Private deploy option 'dedicated-vpc-3' is what Crosstec selected.
- Natalie/Marcus: please confirm the two TODO cells in the exhibit — Ben flagged them.
- Sean: I'll be ready for the legal redline call; happy to run the clause options with your counsel.

HubSpot: I've added the DPA redline task to HubSpot (CROS-5721) and linked the Drive folder.

— Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_DPA_Exhibit_Dataflow.xlsx (spreadsheet, annotated)
